blocks.text: How Enflite plans production and purchasing with **SyteLine APS**: the planner's and the buyer's daily routines, and the forms that explain why an order is late or short.
These pages condense the planning team's daily SOP and the APS training the team uses. The planning team should review them.

topics.subtitle: APS planning and procurement at Enflite
topics.summary: The daily routines for planners and buyers, and the forms that explain the plan.
topics.title: Planning

blocks.text: Your job has two halves: give **APS** accurate input, and act on what it outputs — order suggestions, red flags, and late projections.

items: Enter demand. Create forecasts on the **Forecast** form (quantity, forecast date, warehouse). Maintain **MPS** orders for MPS items on the **Master Production Schedule** form.

Answer APS suggestions. Generate the **Material Planner Workbench**, review the **PLN** lines, select the ready ones, and click **Generate Orders** to create job orders. Review each new job on the **Job Orders** form.
Chase late supply. On **Demand Summary APS**, sort by **Days Late**; open **Demand Detail** to see the critical path and the cause of the delay.
Check capacity. On **Resource Group Utilization APS**, look for utilization over 100%.
Work the exceptions. Filter **Planning Detail** on **Exception Message** (try `Move In Rcpt*`, `Move Out Rcpt*`, or `*` for all), or open the **Exceptions** report.
Clear shortages. Use **Item Bottlenecks APS** and **Component Shortage APS** to find what each job is waiting on; export to Excel and sort by due date.

Sweep past-due jobs. On **Job Orders**, filter **Status** = Released, **Job End Date** earlier than today, **Not Ready** — toggle **Ready** off and on to recheck, and use **Component Shortages** to see the missing material.

Release planned supplies and update the plan. Convert workbench suggestions into orders, resolve planning errors on **APS Planning and Scheduling Messages**, and print the **Dispatch List** for the shop.
Release orders on the **APS** release dates, not early.
Release a job only when all of its material is in inventory.
Do not create shop orders to hedge capacity or projected needs.

topics.summary: The planner's day: enter demand, answer APS suggestions, and chase down late supply.
topics.title: Daily routine: planner

blocks.text: Buyers work the purchasing side of the plan: clear the messages, then convert **APS** order suggestions (**PLN**s) into purchase orders.

items: Clear planning messages. Open **APS Planning and Scheduling Messages** and resolve any errors or warnings from the last planning run.
Run the **Exception Report**. Act on it before creating anything new: receipts you no longer need, purchase orders to move in, purchase orders to move out.
Generate the **Material Planner Workbench** (**Material Planner Workbench Generation**), filtered to purchased items, your buyer code, and the release window.

Review the workbench. The expedite column shows what must be expedited; if a line's presence is unclear, open **Planning Detail** to see the demand and supply behind it. Adjust quantities, combine lines, and pick vendors.

Generate orders. Check **Process Line** (or **Process Through Date**) and click **Generate Orders**. **PLN**s become purchase orders in planned status; several **PLN**s for one vendor roll into a single PO with multiple lines.
Re-run **APS** so the plan recognizes the new supply.

blocks.text: Release each purchase order on its **APS** release date, not early. Early release ties up cash and pulls material and capacity away from higher-priority work.

items: Two **PLN**s for the same item on consecutive days is usually days-supply consolidation (**Planning Parameters**), not a bug.

If a supplier can flex but you cannot say by how much, model a nominal one-day expedited lead time on the item. That raises a proactive expedite message on the workbench instead of a surprise after the PO exists.
